A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a fixed m, the F-dimension function M(m+1,-) is an upper semi-continuous function on the set of all positive integers.
the upper bound for the dimension of a Lie subalgebra R of index m in the full nxn algebra is the maximum of the sum of the m+1 largest numbers in a partition of n.
, for any fixed m, we have found the exact value of the maximum dimension for the Lie nilpotent m-subalgebras of the full matrix algebra over any field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the upper bound for the F-dimension is independent of the characteristic of F.
the Lie nilpotence indices of the subalgebras of the matrix algebra are intimately connected to the dimension of the subalgebra, in a way that is not the case for the associative nilpotence index.
the Lie nilpotent index of an algebra of matrices is a much more delicate invariant than the nilpotent index.
